newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Pakistan to hold talks next week - minister.
newsitem.headline: India, Pakistan to hold talks next week - minister.

text.p: India and Pakistan will hold peace talks next week in New Delhi despite a political crisis threatening Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Friday.
Gujral told Reuters that he would meet his Pakistani counterpart, Gohar Ayub Khan, both during and after a meeting of foreign ministers of the Non-Aligned Movement, set for April 7-8.

Foreign secretaries of the two countries held four days of talks which ended last Monday. It was unclear whether the foreign ministers would go ahead with next week's meetings as Deve Gowda faces a vote of confidence in parliament on April 11.
Asked if he would meet his Pakistani counterpart next week, Gujral said: "Yes, I am looking forward to it and I'm sure when he comes here we'll have the opportunity of getting together."

Gujral, who spoke after addressing senior officials of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), said he and Khan would hold talks on the sidelines of next week's NAM ministerial meeting and also after the conference.

He was asked if they would be able to prepare an agenda for a meeting of the two nations' prime ministers in the Maldives in May. "Yes, definitely because primarily you must keep in mind that governments are ongoing institutions. Whichever government is in office, we will definitely pay attention to this," he said.
